oracle.version: VACASK unstable-2026 (nix store path cjp1w6v1g1s0ih1g13ip8pnkhyygjnl9-vacask-unstable-2026; the binary reports version 'unknown'); device psp103v4.osdi from its lib/vacask/mod: PSP 103.4.0 / JUNCAP 200.5.0 (VACASK devices/psp103v4), compiled by VACASK's OpenVAF-r
oracle.derivation: VACASK run of the benchmark's native circuit, vacask_ring.assets/vacask/runme.sim with its models.inc (the same PSP103 cards as this deck, plus type=+1/-1): tran step=0.05n stop=1u maxstep=0.05n, tran_method="trap", VACASK default tolerances; 26040 accepted points, 1 rejected. Stored binary raw doubles (%.14g), selected by column name: node k -> v(k), vdd:flow(br) -> i(vdd) (the same sign as SPICE: negative while the supply delivers). Transient values retain reference accepted times. Rows: the first 64 and last 64 accepted points, round(k*(N-1)/128) for k = 1..127, and each column's argmin/argmax, the rule the ngspice-derived stress/vacask_* oracles use. Replaces an ngspice-44.2 oracle that ran MOS level 1: ngspice rejects LEVEL 1040, and the migrated deck had lost every card parameter but uo (user-approved regeneration).
oracle.command: vacask -sp -qp runme.sim  (in a copy of vacask_ring.assets/vacask with psp103v4.osdi beside it)

notes: PSP103 cards restored from the benchmark circuit (models.inc without type, which NMOS/PMOS carry); oracle regenerated with VACASK, see oracle.derivation.
